findings.title: Checkout reaches past declared cart boundary into pricing internals

evidence.quote:
`src/cart` owns items and totals, `src/checkout` owns the flow. Pricing and
stock currently import each other through `src/cart/stock.ts`.

findings.note: docs/architecture.md declares cart as sole owner of totals, but checkout's legacy path imports cart/pricing directly and computes a price itself instead of going through cart's total(). Any change to pricing logic (e.g. discounts) must be replicated in checkout to keep the legacy path correct.

open_questions.question: docs/architecture.md describes pricing and stock as importing each other; is that coupling considered acceptable long-term since both live inside the single src/cart package, or is a boundary intended between them?

looks_bad_but_fine.why: cart.ts -> pricing.ts -> stock.ts -> (type-only) cart.ts forms a cycle, but all three files live inside the single src/cart directory/package and the back-edge (src/cart/stock.ts:1) is a type-only import erased at compile time, not a runtime circular dependency. This is an intra-package design smell rather than a cross-module architecture cycle.

not_assessed: Whether the coverageThreshold in package.json (lines: 80) is currently met — no coverage report was available to check.
Whether ESLint or tsc actually flag the pricing/stock cycle — no import-cycle or boundary tooling (e.g. eslint-plugin-import, dependency-cruiser) is configured in .eslintrc.json or package.json.
